About Neighborhood Description:
The Islander Club of Longboat Key is a gated Gulf-front condominium community of two twelve-story towers set on 400 feet of private beachfront along the island's southern half. Both towers are connected by a clubhouse level that serves as the community's social hub. Residences are predominantly two-bedroom, two-bath layouts with open living and dining areas, private balconies, and Gulf or island views, with a handful of larger combined floor plans.

The amenity set centers on the beach. A pool sits directly on the Gulf side with a furnished sun deck. The clubhouse connects the towers and holds a community room, library, game room, and a fitness center. There are also two tennis courts rounding out the grounds.

From this location, St. Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota are just a short drive away, and the island's dining and recreation are minutes away in either direction. The Islander Club is great for those who want direct beachfront living at an established address, with the towers' shared clubhouse giving the community a more social character than most buildings its size.

About Neighborhood Description:
Tangerine Bay Club is a gated, Mediterranean-style community on the Bay-side of Longboat Key's southern end. Its 90 residences are set in elegant low-rise buildings beside a nature preserve with wide views of Sarasota Bay and the downtown skyline beyond.

The amenities here feel like a resort. They include a free-form community pool, clubhouse with kitchen, a fitness center, walking and jogging paths, a tennis court, fishing pier, day dock, and a kayak launch.

The beach is within reach too. Residents may join the Bay Isles Beach Club for a small yearly fee, adding a private stretch of Gulf sand with cabanas and picnic facilities just minutes away. The location seals it: St. Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota are a short drive over the bridge, and the golf and dining of the Longboat Key Club are close by. For buyers who want bayfront resort living with the beach in reach, Tangerine Bay Club is hard to top.

About Neighborhood Description:
Grand Bay is one of the most secluded addresses in Bay Isles: 272 residences in six curved towers on the bay side of Longboat Key, right next to the fairways of the Harbourside golf course and reached through its own gated entry inside the Bay Isles gates. With no more than six residences per floor, homes feature high ceilings, floor-to-ceiling glass, and oversized wraparound terraces framing Sarasota Bay, the golf course, and, from the upper floors, the Gulf itself. Select penthouses capture sunrise over the bay and sunset over the Gulf from one residence.

The community runs a full-service amenity set: on-site management, concierge, and 24/7 access control, with two heated pools, tennis courts, a fitness center, clubhouse, and walking trails through the tropical grounds. Ownership carries deeded membership in the private Bay Isles Beach Club on the Gulf, with optional Longboat Key Club membership adding golf, dining, and marina privileges at The Moorings just around the corner.

Grand Bay suits buyers who want tower living with genuine privacy: double-gated security, low per-floor density, resort amenities, and beach club access included.

About Neighborhood Description:
Lands End occupies one of the most distinctive corners of Longboat Key, a gated enclave of just twelve residences at the island's northern tip. The homes are custom, contemporary designs set among dense tropical landscaping along a natural bayou off Sarasota Bay, a setting that draws wading birds and excellent fishing right to the doorstep. Though the residences live like single-family homes, the community is structured as a condominium association, keeping grounds care off the owner's plate.

Shared amenities are woven into the landscape rather than laid out around a clubhouse. A community pool and a tennis and pickleball court sit hidden in the trees, and common docks on the bayou give owners water access for boating and fishing. The overall feel is quiet and naturalistic, a slice of Old Florida that has become rare on the island.

The setting borders historic Longbeach Village, so the Shore, Mar Vista, and Whitney's are all within an easy stroll, and the Gulf beach is a short walk across the island. Anna Maria Island sits just across the pass to the north, with the rest of Longboat Key's shops and dining down Gulf of Mexico Drive to the south.

About Neighborhood Description:
Harbour Circle is a community of contemporary Spanish-style villas with the Harbourside golf course of the Longboat Key Club as its literal backyard. Villas are mostly three-bedroom, two-and-a-half-bath floor plans, and the neighborhood is walking distance from The Moorings marina.

Harbour Circle is maintenance-free, with the association handling exterior upkeep. Several homes have also added private pools alongside the community pool and spa.

As Bay Isles residents, owners hold deeded membership in the private Bay Isles Beach Club on the Gulf, with optional Longboat Key Club membership adding golf on the course next door, tennis, dining, and marina privileges. Harbour Circle is for those who want single-level villa ease, golf-course surroundings, and the full Bay Isles package at a walkable, central location behind the gates.

About Neighborhood Description:
Silver Sands is a small resort community that sits directly on the Gulf, toward the north end of Longboat Key. The grounds feel like a classic Old Florida beach resort. A community pool sits beside the sand, and lounge chairs and umbrellas wait on the private beach. Owners and guests can play the putting green, try the shuffleboard courts, or grill dinner at the BBQ area, all set among lush tropical gardens.

What sets Silver Sands apart is rental freedom. Nightly and weekly stays are allowed here, and an on-site rental office can handle everything, from bookings to daily maid service. That makes Silver Sands a strong choice for buyers who want their beach home to earn income when they're away. The north-end location adds to the appeal, with the shops of Longbeach Village close by and Anna Maria Island just across the bridge.

About Neighborhood Description:
Inn on the Beach is a gated beachfront condominium community at the southern tip of Longboat Key. The community of roughly 221 residences offers one-bedroom and two-bedroom floor plans, with many units looking out over the Gulf of Mexico or the Longboat Key Club golf course. The white sand is steps from the buildings and St. Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota are just a short drive away.

What makes Inn on the Beach unique on the island is its dual identity as both a residential community and a resort. Owners can place their units in the resort's rental program and receive approximately half the revenue their unit generates from resort guests, or simply live in their residence full or part time. Flexible leasing with short minimum stays makes this one of the most rental-friendly ownership structures on Longboat Key, and concierge service comes with the resort setting.

Residents enjoy a heated pool, fitness center, and beach access within the community, along with the gated Longboat Key Club setting. Membership in the Longboat Key Club is optional and opens up 45 holes of golf, an award-winning tennis center, a full-service spa, dining, and the club's deep-water marina. Inn on the Beach suits buyers who want a beachfront residence with genuine income potential, or a lock-and-leave that lives like a resort.

About Neighborhood Description:
Bayou Hammock is a small, quiet neighborhood located toward the north end of Longboat Key. It’s known for its tucked-away feel and larger homesites compared to many areas on the island. Streets are low traffic, and the neighborhood has more of an “Old Florida” residential character rather than a planned or amenity-driven layout.

Properties here often sit on oversized lots with mature landscaping, creating a strong sense of privacy. Some homes offer water access or canal frontage, while others are valued primarily for land size and redevelopment potential. Because of the larger parcels, Bayou Hammock can attract buyers looking to renovate or build new construction in a less dense setting.

The north-key location places residents close to Longboat Key’s quieter beaches and village areas while still within driving distance of Anna Maria Island and St. Armands. Buyers seeking space, privacy, and a non-HOA feel often gravitate toward this neighborhood.

About Neighborhood Description:
Country Club Shores is the southernmost single-family neighborhood on Longboat Key - a classic boater's community built around 20 deep-water canals with private docks and quick access to Sarasota Bay. Homes range from original Florida ranch houses to newly built waterfront estates, with open-bayfront lots commanding the premium positions.

The neighborhood keeps its amenities simple - deeded beach access across Gulf of Mexico Drive and an association that maintains the common areas. Many Longboat Key Club amenities like golf sit directly across the street, with optional membership adding 45 holes of championship golf, tennis, spa, dining, and marina privileges. It's resort living by proximity rather than obligation: close enough to use, with no requirement to join.

Country Club Shores suits boaters first - backyard dockage with the Gulf minutes away is the defining feature - along with buyers who want a pet-friendly,  single-family neighborhood at the island's south end, just minutes from St. Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota, with monthly rental flexibility for seasonal owners.

About Neighborhood Description:
The Residences at The St. Regis Longboat Key is a resort-style Gulf-front community of 69 homes in south Longboat Key. Residences range from one to four bedrooms across 18 floor plans, and each one is reached by private elevator with keyless entry. Floor to ceiling glass, soaring ceilings, and oversized terraces frame the water, and many homes look straight out over the Gulf.

Owners have a private world inside the resort. The Resident Clubhouse holds a residents-only fitness center and lounge, and the Resident's Beach Club offers cabanas, preferred chaise lounges, and a Gulf-front pool. Butler and concierge service extends into every residence, ready for each member of the family.

The five-star resort completes the picture. Residents can enjoy the spa and salon, chef-driven restaurants, casual beachside dining, multiple pools, and a saltwater lagoon, all steps from home. St. Armands Circle is a short drive south, with downtown Sarasota just across the bridge.

About Neighborhood Description:
Seaplace is one of the largest communities on Longboat Key, with more than 400 residences spread across 42 acres. The grounds feel like a park with two mid-rise towers with garden buildings set among lawns and fountains, two mid-rise towers, and a small collection of townhomes. A half mile of private Gulf beach runs along the western edge, with chaise lounges and umbrellas waiting on the sand.

The amenities here are like a resort. The community features 2 heated pools, 3 tennis courts, a fitness center, walking trails through the grounds, and a remodeled clubhouse. A guarded gate also covers the entrance.

Being on the south-end of Longboat Key is also great. Golfing is just across the street (with an optional Longboat Key Club membership) and a variety of shops are just minutes away along with St Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota.

Being on the south end of Longboat Key, the Pierre is within arm's reach of many optional Longboat Key Club amenities including golf, dining, pickleball and more.

About Neighborhood Description:
Buttonwood Harbor is a beautiful neighborhood of estates that are tucked away on the Bay side of Longboat Key. Quiet streets wind along the canals of Buttonwood Harbor and Cranes Bayou. The neighborhood is made up of single-family homes ranging from well-kept Old Florida ranch houses to newer elevated custom builds, all set among mature oaks and palms.

Boating is the heart of Buttonwood Harbor. Homes on the water feature private docks with deep-water access to Sarasota Bay, and the homeowners association maintains a community boat basin and ramp with dockage available to residents whose homes are off the water. The boat basin also serves as the community's social hub, hosting potlucks and casual get-togethers through the year.

Everyday conveniences are close by, with a grocery-anchored shopping plaza right near the neighborhood entrance and public beach access a short distance away.

About Neighborhood Description:
Dream Island is one of Longboat Key's quietest waterfront addresses - a small enclave of single-family homes set on deep-water canals on the bay side of the island. The neighborhood mixes original Florida homes with newer custom construction, on some of the largest residential lots on the Key - half-acre-plus parcels with 100+ feet of protected waterfront are part of the community's fabric.

This is boating-first living without the resort wrapper: private docks and lifts in the backyard and Sarasota Bay minutes away by water. There are no community amenities, gates, or shared facilities - the appeal is elbow room, privacy, and dockage, with the Gulf beach a short walk across Gulf of Mexico Drive.

Dream Island suits those who want estate-scale canal-front property and serious boating access in a low-key setting - including those looking to build, since oversized lots here periodically come to market as teardown or new-construction opportunities.

About Neighborhood Description:
Sleepy Lagoon is a single-family neighborhood at the north end of Longboat Key. It stretches across both sides of Gulf of Mexico Drive, from bayside canals all the way to the Gulf beach. The community holds around 270 homes in a wide mix of styles, from large new waterfront estates to classic Old Florida cottages and ranch homes. There are no condo towers here, just gorgeous residential streets shaded by tropical landscaping.

Water is the heart of the neighborhood. On the Bay side, homes line a series of canals - giving residents access to Sarasota Bay with many having private docks. On the Gulf side, homes enjoy a private beach experience from their backyard while anyone from Sleepy Lagoon can also enjoy separately deeded beach access.

Life here is simple by design. The shops and restaurants of Longbeach Village are just up the road, Anna Maria Island is across the bridge, and groceries and dining at the Centre Shops are a short drive south. For buyers who want boating, beach, and a true island neighborhood in one place, Sleepy Lagoon delivers.

Aria is best suited for buyers seeking a newer construction, boutique-style lifestyle with strong wellness and social amenities. Compared to older Longboat Key luxury towers, it appeals to those prioritizing modern design and privacy.

About Neighborhood Description:
Conrad Beach is a boutique single-family neighborhood of just 27 homes, designed in a cohesive coastal style with a strong architectural identity. The neighborhood features Key West–inspired homes with metal roofs, elevated construction, and colorful island design elements. It’s one of the few areas on Longboat Key that blends single-family ownership with lawn-maintenance as part of the HOA.

Conrad Beach appeals to buyers who want the privacy of a home without the full workload of exterior upkeep. Streets are pedestrian-friendly, and the uniform design gives the neighborhood a polished, resort-like feel. Other amenities include a community pool and beautiful walking paths throughout the neighborhood.

Located on the north end of the island, Conrad Beach offers convenient access to the beach along with close proximity to Longbeach Village dining.

The Players Club is an exclusive luxury condominium community set right on the water on the south end of Longboat Key. Made up of 134 residences in 4 mid-rise buildings, the community offers a full suite of amenities along with generous green space between buildings, preserving the resort feel of the grounds.

A large heated pool and spa anchor the outdoor scene, 4 Har-Tru tennis/pickleball courts and a putting green cover the sporting side, and the clubhouse brings residents together with a fitness center, entertainment space, catering kitchen, and library. The south-end location is one of the island's most convenient. Everyday services are just a short drive away and places like St. Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota are just across the bridge.

Villa di Lancia is a gated Gulf-front community of 38 residences in two Mediterranean style buildings on the south end of Longboat Key. Five acres of landscaped grounds run down to a private beachfront. The homes here are some of the largest beachfront condominiums on the island - running from about 2,400 to nearly 5,000 square feet. These homes come with high ceilings and big terraces.

The amenities match the scale. A heated Gulf-side pool with a lap area sits beside an 11-person hot tub, and two Har-Tru tennis courts are lined for pickleball as well. The clubhouse holds a fitness room and a sauna, and the clubroom's full kitchen makes hosting easy. Garden paths wind the grounds, and building staff handle the day to day. Each home also comes with under building parking and storage.

The south end location keeps the island's best within reach. The Shoppes of Bay Isles with Publix and a pharmacy are just up the road, and golf and tennis at the Longboat Key Club are minutes away. St. Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota are a short drive south.

About Neighborhood Description:
Jewfish Key is a private island of roughly 38 acres in the Intracoastal Waterway off the northern tip of Longboat Key. The island is reachable only by boat, with Longboat Key's marinas and restaurant docks just a few minutes away.

Homes here occupy generous lots of an acre or more and roughly half the island is preserved as natural habitat. Homes are elevated with panoramic water views, and private docks put Sarasota Bay right outside the door. The sandbar on the island's western side - a popular gathering spot for area boaters - is also a nearby option.

Life on Jewfish Key trades drive-up convenience for a privacy that exists nowhere else on Longboat Key. Groceries, dining, and errands run by boat to north Longboat Key and Anna Maria Island. Jewfish Key suits buyers for whom the boat ride is the point: true private island living just minutes from everything.

About Neighborhood Description:
With just 8 residences, Seascape is one of the smallest condominium communities on Longboat Key. This community sits directly on the Gulf, near the midpoint of the island. Every home is a spacious three-bedroom, two-bath residence with about 1,500 square feet of living space.

Simple is the point here.  The grounds are well-kept, with brick paver walkways and lush tropical landscaping. A pool sits between the building and the sand, and lounge chairs wait on the beach just steps away. Each residence comes with two assigned covered parking spaces under the building, plus extra storage. Seascape is lease-friendly, making it a flexible choice for seasonal owners.

The mid-key location puts the whole island within easy reach. The island trolley stops along Gulf of Mexico Drive, and St. Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota are a short drive south. To the north, the shops and restaurants of historic Longbeach Village offer a taste of old Florida. For buyers who want a quiet, private home right on the beach, Seascape is a great find.

About Neighborhood Description:
Emerald Harbor is a bayside enclave of 82 homes on the north end of Longboat Key, spread across three quiet streets — Emerald Harbor Drive, Binnacle Point Drive, and Old Compass Road. The neighborhood was designed around its signature feature: the widest lagoon-style canals on Longboat Key, deep enough for sailboat keels and yachts up to 60 feet, with direct, bridge-free access to Sarasota Bay and the Intracoastal Waterway.

Homes sit on generously sized lots and range from original old-Florida ranches to newer Key West and Mediterranean-style construction built to modern flood and hurricane standards. Residents also enjoy the amenity most canal neighborhoods can't offer: private deeded beach access directly across Gulf of Mexico Drive, maintained by the neighborhood's voluntary association.

Emerald Harbor suits boaters first, especially those with larger vessels who need canal width and depth that most of the island can't accommodate. It also fits buyers seeking oversized waterfront lots for new construction, in an established neighborhood with a relaxed, residential feel.

The Bayou is a neighborhood of 126 custom single-family homes tucked behind two sets of gates in Bay Isles. 49 homes sit on the Bay Isles Waterway. Many of these waterfront homes have their own docks with a protected run out to Sarasota Bay.  Other homes line the golf course or have lake views.

The neighborhood holds regular social events to connect neighbors. Events include the annual St. Pat's Day Dog Parade and various parties at the Bay Isles Beach Club. Every owner gets deeded access to that private stretch of Gulf beach, with a covered pavilion, picnic tables, grills, and an on-site attendant.

Optional membership to the Longboat Key Club opens up championship golf, tennis, club dining, and the Moorings marina. Publix, CVS, the library, and the town center sit just outside the north gate, with St. Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota a short drive south.

About Neighborhood Description:
Laguna Yacht Village is one of Longboat Key's smallest and most private communities, a gated enclave of just 8 homes on the island's north end. Though the homes live like single-family residences, the community is structured as a condominium, so grounds maintenance, the private road, and shared amenities are handled by the association.

Boating is at the heart of Laguna Yacht Village. Each home includes a deeded deep-water dock in a protected lagoon just minutes from the Intracoastal Waterway and the Gulf of Mexico, with no fixed bridges along the way. A heated community pool and spa round out the shared amenities, and deeded beach access directly across Gulf of Mexico Drive puts the sand within a short walk.

The north-end location keeps things quiet while staying connected. Restaurants, shops, and a full-service marina are close by on the island, and the beaches and dining of Anna Maria Island are a short drive north.

About Neighborhood Description:
Windward Bay sits along Sarasota Bay on the north end of Longboat Key. The community is a mix of low-rise condominiums and a cluster of single-story villas. Homes run from about 900 square feet up to about 1,900, and many look straight out over the water.

Boating is the draw here. Deep-water slips line the seawall, available to rent as they open up, with water and power at the dock. There is a fishing pier with cleaning stations, plus kayak storage and a launch. On land, two heated pools serve the community, and the clubhouse holds a kitchen and a library. Residents also have a fitness room, saunas, two tennis courts, shuffleboard, and half a mile of walking paths along the bay.

Ownership carries deeded access to the Gulf beach, just across the street. A nature preserve backs the southern edge of the property, which keeps that side quiet. Grills, fire pits, and picnic tables are set out along the water. The community welcomes pets. Two are allowed, and one can weigh up to 75 pounds.

About Neighborhood Description:
Sea Pines is a place of quiet seclusion.  A community of 28 condos directly on the beach at the northern tip of Longboat Key, this area is much less dense than other parts of the island. Homes here are two-bedroom floor plans - many with dens, screened lanais, and Gulf views past the dunes.

Life at Sea Pines centers on the sand and the pool. A large heated pool sits among lush tropical grounds, with the private beach path just steps away. Sea Pines is also one of the friendliest communities on the island for dog owners - two dogs are welcome, even large breeds. Owners can also lease their homes up to six times a year with a one-month minimum.

The north-end location is a walker's dream. The Village and its beloved restaurants are a walk away while Whitney Plaza and Anna Maria Island are a short drive away.

About Neighborhood Description:
Sutton Place is a Gulf-to-Bay community near the middle of Longboat Key. About 80 residences share six acres of tropical grounds on the Bay side of the island, in a mix of condominiums, duplexes, and villas. Many homes enjoy views over Sarasota Bay, and the friendly, social feel of the neighborhood is one of its biggest draws.

The Bay-side grounds are packed with amenities. Two heated pools anchor the community, along with an expansive clubhouse with a library, billiards, and a kitchen. Boaters love the owner's marina, where docks can be leased, and the kayak storage with an electric launch. Fishing piers, a fish-cleaning station, gas grills, and a car wash station round things out, with an on-site handyman and management team keeping it all in top shape.

The beach side is what makes Sutton Place extra special. Residents own beach access directly across Gulf of Mexico Drive, complete with a pavilion, picnic tables, restrooms with hot showers, lockers for beach chairs, and parking. Bayfront Park and its courts are moments away and the Publix at Bay Isles is a few minutes south. Few communities on the island put the Bay and the beach this close together at this price of entry.

About Neighborhood Description:
Bayview Estates is a single-family waterfront neighborhood on the north end of Longboat Key, tucked into the Sleepy Lagoon area on the bay side of the island. Most homes here sit directly on deep-water canals with private docks and seawalls, and the canals connect to Bishop's Bayou and the Intracoastal Waterway. For those who prefer a private home and yard over condominium living, it's one of the island's most complete boating neighborhoods.

The homes themselves span decades - from renovated Old Florida residences to newer custom builds constructed on the same canal lots. That mix gives Bayview Estates a wider range of architectural styles and living experiences than the island's condominium communities, while the atmosphere stays established, upscale and quietly residential.

Despite the bayside setting, the Gulf is hardly an afterthought - the public beach access is very close by. It's the rare Longboat Key arrangement where you can walk to the beach in the morning and take the boat out from your backyard in the afternoon.

Emerald Pointe is a private enclave of just 22 residences within the gates of Bay Isles, set on a pair of quiet cul-de-sacs off Harbourside Drive on south Longboat Key. It's really two sibling communities: Emerald Pointe South, with 16 homes, and Emerald Pointe North - the smallest community in all of Bay Isles at just six residences, each with views of the Longboat Key Club's Harbourside golf course.

These are freestanding two-story homes with courtyards, private pools and lanais, high ceilings, and two-plus-car garages - maintenance-free living in a detached-home format. Ownership is condominium-form despite the freestanding design, which helps keep insurance costs down while the association handles exterior upkeep. Floor plans run to roughly 2,500 square feet in the South and up to 3,600 in the North.

As Bay Isles residents, owners are automatically members of the private Bay Isles Beach Club - a gated Gulf-front beach parcel with pavilions, grills, restrooms, and volleyball about a half mile away - with optional Longboat Key Club membership adding golf, tennis, fitness, spa, and marina privileges at The Moorings. Emerald Pointe suits those who want newer construction and lock-and-leave ease inside the island's premier gated master community.

About Neighborhood Description:
Longbeach Village is where Longboat Key began. The island's first homestead was settled here, and the neighborhood - called simply "the Village" by locals - carries a state historic designation, with some structures standing for more than a century. Its shell-lined streets hold an eclectic mix of original cottages, mid-century bungalows and renovated coastal homes. There is no HOA, no gate, and no fee - an increasingly rare arrangement on the island that gives Longbeach Village its individuality.

Life here centers on the water and the walk. Restaurants are just a walk away within this neighborhood and a public boat ramp puts boats into the bay minutes from Longboat Pass and the Gulf. Waterfront homes along the Village's canals and bayfront carry private docks, the popular sandbar off Jewfish Key sits just offshore, and the white sand of Whitney Beach is a short walk across the island.

The northern tip location adds one more advantage: the bridge to Anna Maria Island is right at the Village's doorstep, opening up restaurants and shops, while the rest of Longboat Key stretches south.

About Neighborhood Description:
Regent Court is an enclave of just 8 spacious luxury estate homes on the south end of Longboat Key. Each home sits on a large Gulf-front parcel of an acre or more, tucked between the beach and the Islandside golf course. These are some of the largest homes on the island, with wide private beach frontage and sweeping Gulf views.

There are no shared amenities here - and that's the point. Each estate is built as its own private retreat, and most include private pools and large outdoor living spaces. Homes in Regent Court rarely come on the market. When they do, they draw some of the highest prices on the Key.

Membership to the Longboat Key Club is optional and close at hand. It opens up championship golf, tennis, a full-service marina, and club dining. St. Armands Circle and its shops and restaurants are a short drive south. Downtown Sarasota's arts and waterfront are just beyond.

About Neighborhood Description:
The Harbour Villa Club is a 38-residence bayfront condominium community tucked onto Dream Island Road, just off Gulf of Mexico Drive on the quiet north end of Longboat Key. The community sits directly on Sarasota Bay and was designed so residences capture bay views from both the living area and the primary bedroom. Units are two-bedroom, two-bath layouts, many with lanais that open to the bay breeze, and each comes with a carport and a deeded boat slip.

Boating is the headline here. The community's deep-water marina can accommodate vessels in the 50 to 60 foot range, there is a boat ramp on site, and the north-end location puts the Intracoastal Waterway and the Gulf a short run from the dock. Back on land, residents share a large heated pool with a spacious sun deck and poolside grill, a ten-person spa, and lighted tennis courts.

Harbour Villa Club is a practical fit for boaters, seasonal residents, and owners who want income potential.

About Neighborhood Description:
La Firenza is one of the most intimate Gulf-front addresses on Longboat Key. Just 10 residences in a pair of four-story Spanish colonial revival buildings. Behind the gated entry, each building holds only 5 homes, and living here is routinely compared to single-family life. Residences run roughly 3,500 to 4,800 square feet with expansive wraparound terraces, summer kitchens and floor-to-ceiling glass framing Gulf views. Every unit includes a private two-car or three-car garage under the building, with elevator service up from the climate-controlled parking level.

Amenities here include resort-style pool, a clubhouse, catering kitchen and fitness facilities with a sauna. From the pool deck, a pavered path and boardwalk leads directly onto 350 feet of private beach reserved for residents and their guests, framed by lush tropical landscaping throughout the grounds.

The mid-key setting keeps daily life easy. The island's Publix and shopping plazas are minutes away and Membership at the Longboat Key Club is optional for residents who want golf and other club amenities. La Firenza is perfect for those who want the space and privacy of an estate home with the lock-and-leave simplicity of a condominium, in a community small enough that every neighbor is known.

About Neighborhood Description:
Whitney Beach sits at the north end of Longboat Key and spans both sides of Gulf of Mexico Drive. Most homes line Bishop's Bayou on the bay side, in low-rise buildings and single-story villas. A separate group of residences sits across the road on the Gulf side, right on the sand. Homes run from about 940 square feet up to about 1,500, with one, two, and three bedrooms.

Two docks reach out into Bishop's Bayou, with boat slips for resident boats and a boathouse to gather in. From there it's a clear run to Sarasota Bay with no bridges. There is also a fishing dock and kayak launch with storage. Two heated pools serve the bay side, and a third sits on the Gulf side.

Across the road, the Conservancy is private land the community owns. Residents and their guests walk through it to reach a wide, quiet stretch of Gulf beach. The Conservancy also holds a play area, picnic tables, shuffleboard, and tennis courts striped for pickleball. Owners may rent their homes for a month at a time, up to six times a year, and the Longbeach Village shops and restaurants are just up the road.

Northgate of Longboat Key sits at the island's quiet northern tip. This boutique waterfront condo community holds just 9 residences in a small midrise directly on the water.

A community pool anchors the shared outdoor space, residents have their own clay tennis court, and three small docks make it easy to launch a kayak, paddleboard, or small boat right from home. The north end lifestyle is the real amenity. The white sand beach waits at the end of North Shore Road, and the village's beloved restaurants are a short walk or bike ride away. Anna Maria Island's shops and beaches sit just across the bridge as well.

About Neighborhood Description:
The Shore is a Gulf-front community of just over 50 residences near the north end of Longboat Key. The homes are surrounded by tropical grounds that run down to a wide stretch of private beach.

The shared spaces cover a lot for a community this size. Amenities include a heated pool and hot tub, a sauna, a gym, and a spacious social room with a full kitchen. Each home comes with assigned covered parking and a large private storage room for beach gear. Best of all for dog lovers, The Shore is one of the few communities on the island that welcomes large pets.

The north end location puts daily life close at hand. Restaurants, shops, services, and bay access are all just minutes away. Anna Maria Island is an easy drive north, and Longbeach Village is up the road.

The Aquarius Club is a direct Gulf-front, boutique-style condominium on the south end of Longboat Key, known for offering a full set of daily-use amenities without feeling like a massive resort tower. Residents are drawn to the ease of true beachfront living paired with well-maintained common areas designed for both social gatherings and everyday routines.

On the amenity side, the Aquarius Club features a heated Gulf-front pool, two Har-Tru tennis courts (with pickleball referenced by some community sources), a state-of-the-art fitness center, and a clubroom with a catering kitchen and social meeting space. Outdoor areas support entertaining with grilling and patio seating, and the building also provides on-site management with concierge-style service elements.

From a buyer’s perspective, the Aquarius Club fits those seeking true beachfront living, a resort-like amenity package, and a community scale that still feels personal.

About Neighborhood Description:
Weston Pointe is a small enclave of 15 homes behind the gates of Bay Isles on the south end of Longboat Key. The same architectural firm designed every home, which gives the street a consistent look. Each one has a two-car garage and a private pool set in a walled courtyard.

Boating is the draw here. Every home comes with an assigned boat slip in the community marina basin, with water and power at the dock. From there it's a straight run to Sarasota Bay through the Bay Isles perimeter canal, with no bridges in the way, and the Gulf is a short cruise beyond. The association handles the yard work, the grounds, and the pools. These are single-family homes on their own lots, so you get the space and privacy of a house without the upkeep.

Weston Pointe is the closest Bay Isles neighborhood to the island's town center, which puts Publix, CVS, banks, and the post office within easy reach. The Longboat Key Club Moorings marina and the Harbourside golf course are also just a short walk away. Ownership includes membership in the private Bay Isles Beach Club on the Gulf, and a staffed gate covers the community around the clock. Membership to the Longboat Key Club is optional and adds golf, tennis, fitness, and dining.

About Neighborhood Description:
Harbour Links is one of the smallest communities in Bay Isles - just 20 residences overlooking the Harbourside golf course of the Longboat Key Club. Homes offer great floor plans, private garages and beautiful golf course vistas. Even wireless internet and streaming are included in the association package.

The setting is quiet, low-density Bay Isles living at its most understated: no towers, no crowds, just a small circle of residences behind the gates with the fairways as the back yard. Maintenance-free convenience keeps it lock-and-leave friendly for seasonal owners.

As Bay Isles residents, owners hold deeded membership in the private Bay Isles Beach Club on the Gulf, with optional Longboat Key Club membership adding golf on the course next door, tennis, dining, and marina privileges at The Moorings just around the corner. Harbour Links is for those who want an intimate, golf-view address with the full Bay Isles package and minimal upkeep.

About Neighborhood Description:
Hideaway Bay is one of the most secluded enclaves on Longboat Key, a small single-family community reached by a winding, mangrove-lined road on the island's north end. Homes sit on a quiet peninsula along Millar Bay, adjacent to the Intracoastal Waterway, with water views that take in Sarasota Bay. Custom residences here occupy generous tropical lots, many with private pools, spacious lanais, and multi-car garages.

The waterfront is the draw. Homes enjoy deep-water dockage with boat and jet-ski lifts, no bridges between the docks and the bay, and many properties can accommodate yachts up to the 50 foot range. From the dock it is a short run to the Intracoastal and the Gulf. Community tennis/pickleball courts nearby and underground utilities round out the neighborhood infrastructure.

Despite the hidden-away feel, the essentials are close. Public beach access on the Gulf is close, and Longbeach Village's waterfront restaurants sit just up the road. Membership at the Longboat Key Club is optional for residents who want golf, tennis, dining, and club amenities on the south end. Hideaway Bay suits buyers who want privacy, deep-water boating from their own backyard, and a small neighborhood.

About Neighborhood Description:
L'Ambiance is one of the signature addresses on Longboat Key: twin ten-story Gulf-front towers behind the gates of the Longboat Key Club on the island's south end, set on 18 lushly landscaped acres with roughly 1,000 feet of private beach. Residences have private elevator foyers and are built as free-standing units with no common walls between neighbors.

The amenity package runs deeper than nearly any building on the island: a resort-style heated pool and spa on an expansive deck between the towers, two private Har-Tru tennis courts, a fitness center with sauna and steam rooms, club rooms and social spaces, guest suites for visiting family, concierge service, 24-hour security with a guard gate, on-site management, and under-building secured parking with storage. The grounds greet residents with fountains, palms, and flowering gardens.

Living at L'Ambiance also means living beside the Longboat Key Club, where optional membership adds championship golf, the tennis center, spa, dining, and marina privileges. Shopping in St. Armands Circle and downtown Sarasota is a short drive south. L'Ambiance suits buyers who want exceptional living with a private-residence feel, on one of the most established stretches of beachfront on Longboat Key.

About Neighborhood Description:
Spanish Main Yacht Club is a waterfront villa community on the Bay side of Longboat Key. The community offers over 200 villas - many with beautiful water views. It's a 55+ active adult community with social events happening constantly throughout the year.

Boating is the heart of life here. A private 40-slip deep-water marina sits right on Sarasota Bay, with slips available to residents at modest annual fees and a kayak launch nearby. From the docks, Sarasota Bay is immediately accessible. Back on land, a heated pool overlooks the marina basin, and the clubhouse hosts a full calendar from game nights and book club to fish fries and holiday parties. Shuffleboard courts round out the grounds.

The location keeps everything close. Deeded beach access sits just across Gulf of Mexico Drive, so the Gulf sunsets are a short stroll from any villa. Shopping and dining at the Centre Shops are close by and Longbeach Village is just up the road. For buyers who want boating, neighbors, and a friendly social atmosphere, Spanish Main delivers a lifestyle that is hard to match on the island.

About Neighborhood Description:
En Provence is one of Longboat Key's true boutique ultra-luxury addresses: just 21 residences in three French Mediterranean-style buildings on roughly six acres of direct Gulf-front near the island's south end. Each building holds seven homes on four floors above private enclosed garages - and the residences live like beachfront estates, with floor plans from 3,400 to over 6,000 square feet, private elevators opening into each foyer, and six units with their own private pool courtyards.

The amenity set matches the scale: a heated resort-style pool and spa steps from the sand, a fitness center, and a clubhouse with dining room, catering kitchen, and lounge with bar - plus a full-time concierge and 24-hour gated, guarded security. Fees carry an unusually complete load, covering building exterior and roof, building insurance, grounds, management, security, trash, and water/sewer.

With only 21 owners, inventory is genuinely scarce - units surface rarely and draw serious attention when they do. En Provence suits buyers who want the space and privacy of a beachfront mansion without the upkeep: estate-scale living, delivered in lock-and-leave condominium form.

About Neighborhood Description:
Winding Oaks is a community of duplex condominiums behind the Bay Isles gates in Longboat Key. Each condominium comes with its own two-car garage. Homes run from about 2,000 square feet up to about 2,700. Open floor plans, high ceilings, and wide screened lanais are standard, and many homes look out over a lagoon or the Harbourside golf course.

The setting does a lot of the work here. The community pool sits at the center of the community, ringed by a beautiful nature park. Many homes also have a walled private courtyard, and some owners have added a pool and spa of their own.

Winding Oaks keeps one of the fullest social calendars on the island. Neighbors gather at the pool and at the beach. Activities and clubs are plentiful. They include book clubs, writing clubs, gaming clubs, monthly lunches, group outings, and an end-of-season party. The association handles the roofs, the exterior paint, the grounds, and the building insurance, so owners can lock the door and travel. Ownership includes membership in the private Bay Isles Beach Club on the Gulf, and membership to the Longboat Key Club is optional, adding golf, tennis, fitness, and dining.

The Grande at Longboat Key is an intimate Gulf-front building of just 8 residences near the middle of the island. The Water Club is a gated Gulf-front community of two towers rising over stunning beachfront near the south end of Longboat Key. In most residences, keyed elevator access opens into the home's own private foyer, and inside, ten foot ceilings and walls of glass frame views of the Gulf and the bay.

About Neighborhood Description:
It's rare to have a community spanning both sides of the island and Pelican Harbour & Beach Club is one such community on Longboat Key.  Low-rise condominiums and townhome-style residences sit on both sides of Gulf of Mexico Drive. Bay-view homes along Sarasota Bay enjoy the boating access, while Gulf-side residences are just steps from the private beach.

The amenity list runs long for a community this relaxed. All residents share the community's own Gulf beachfront, and the Bay side hosts a pool, tennis and pickleball courts, a clubhouse, a day dock, boat slips available to residents, and storage space for kayaks. Covered carports add everyday convenience, and the community is pet-friendly.

Situated in the middle of Longboat Key, the location puts everything within reach. Bayfront Park's recreation facilities and dog park are close by. Publix and the island's everyday services are also a short drive away.

About Neighborhood Description:
Set on the shore of Sarasota Bay, Fairway Bay is a gorgeous bayfront community behind the gates of Bay Isles. The community spans mid-rise residences and townhouse-style condominiums with private oversized garages.

Amenities here are one of the deepest in Bay Isles: a community clubhouse with full kitchen, two courts for tennis and pickleball, exercise facilities, pools, a kayak launch, and a shell walking path bordering the bay. Just as notable is the social calendar - the association hosts friendship gatherings, on-site yoga, bridge, mahjong, and book clubs - and every owner holds deeded membership in the private Bay Isles Beach Club on the Gulf, less than a mile away.

Fairway Bay is for those who want gated, resort-level living with a genuine community feel. Combined with its bay views, an active social scene, and Beach Club access, the community is a complete package.
